subject: Post-demo: alignment on goals & proposed test matrix
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@nychealth.org>, Mark Liu <mark.liu@nychealth.org>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Post-demo: alignment on goals & proposed test matrix

Hi Elena / Mark —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of operational tests so we can run a fair side-by-side against the other vendors you're considering.

Pain points we heard today (please flag if I missed anything):
- Inference cost is unpredictable across long-running routing and peak windows.
- Latency spikes during concurrent charting workflows (p95 spikes impacting clinician UX).
- Need strict data residency + audit logs for patient PII access.
- Desire for deterministic model outputs for templated summary tasks (reduce hallucinations).

Primary goals you articulated:
1) Keep p95 latency under 250ms for typical 32-token completions in the clinician workflow.
2) Reduce per-transaction inference cost by >=30% vs current baseline without sacrificing quality.
3) Ensure auditability: token-level audit log + retention for 1 year.

Proposed vendor test matrix (high level) — this is what we'll run in the two-week bake-off:
- Latency: p50/p90/p95 for 32-token and 128-token profiles; 50 concurrent connections simulated.
- Throughput: sustained RPS until TLB/backpressure shows degradation (report steady-state throughput).
- Cost: normalized cost per 1K tokens under the test config (include batch settings).
- Cache behavior: KV/prefix cache hit rates with our medical templating workload.
- Quality: 40 curated prompts across triage/summaries — metrics: ROUGE-L, exact field extraction accuracy, and a small human pass/fail check (4 raters).
- Compliance: confirmation of KMS/HSM support, VPC connectivity checklist, and audit-log format.

Attachments: I uploaded a sample of the patient records we'll use (anonymized rows) and a blank vendor test template to the shared Drive (link below).

Next steps I suggest:
1) We (Redwood) prepare the full test plan + runbook by EOD tomorrow.
2) Aditya will define the exact load scripts and infra commands required for access.
3) Mark / Elena to confirm the test window (we recommended Jun 7–20) and provide a short-lived service account for secure ingestion.
4) Mid-bakeoff checkpoint on June 14 to review interim results.

If that all looks right, I’ll send the finalized test template and request the access details.

Thanks — looking forward to running the side-by-side.

—
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0218

Subject: Re: Post-demo: alignment on goals & proposed test matrix

Camila — thanks for the clear write-up. High level this matches what we talked about. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency target: 250ms p95 is our aspirational target for the clinician microflow. For the batch summarization jobs (128-token), 500ms p95 is acceptable.
2) For the quality evals, we want to prioritize extraction accuracy for the fields: diagnosis_code, medication_list, and follow_up_action.
3) Compliance: our security team needs to confirm audit-log format — I attached a sample of the format they expect.

We'll attach a short-lived service account and a small set of synthetic patient rows to the Drive folder tonight. Please ensure your team treats them as sensitive — they're anonymized but still covered by our data handling policies.

One more ask: can you include the incumbent vendor (Vendor A) and Nimbus AI in the test matrix? We want a three-way head-to-head.

Thanks —
Elena

Attachments: nyc_patient_sample_rows.csv (anonymized)

Elena / Mark — perfect, thanks for the samples and the note on the extraction fields. We'll fold Vendor A and Nimbus AI into the plan.

I attached the vendor test template (blank) to the Drive folder and put a short priorities doc in the same location: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1NYC-POC-plan

Summary of what Redwood will run (details & runbook by EOD tomorrow):
- Load profiles: 50 concurrent clinical sessions for microflow (32 tokens), and a 10‑node batch run for 128-token summarization with 100 parallel jobs.
- Cost calc: we will run each vendor under the same workload and report cost normalized to per-1K tokens including infra egress and any orchestration overhead.
- Quality: we’ll run the 40 prompts and deliver both automated metrics and 6 blinded human ratings for a final pass/fail.
- Compliance: we will collect audit logs and provide a sample of the token-level log format for your security team to vet.

Action items for you: please confirm the test window (we proposed Jun 7–20) and share the short-lived service account (minimum scope: S3 read to sample folder or access key just for the test dataset).

Camila

Thanks Camila — technical notes / proposed test-run commands from my side. I’ll own the infra runbook during the test window.

Test harness basics:
- We’ll use a small k8s cluster for load generation (k6 + custom runners). For consistency we’ll pin sequence lengths and temperature to match your prod prompts.
- Latency test: 10k warmup calls, then 1 minute steady-state with 50 concurrent clients. Collect p50/p90/p95/p99 and token counts.
- Throughput: ramp until 10% error budget is consumed (retries counted), compare sustained throughput between vendors.
- Cache tests: we’ll pre-warm a set of 5K patient prefixes and measure KV cache hit ratio.

Commands (examples):
- Load: ./run_load.sh --profile clinician-32 --clients 50 --duration 60 --target 10000
- Batch: ./run_batch.sh --profile batch-128 --nodes 10 --parallel 100

Data & access ask: please provide an S3 read-only key scoped to s3://nychealth-tests/poctest (short-lived). If you prefer, we can accept temporary signed URLs for the data bundles.

Security: we’ll only ingest the provided anonymized rows; all runs will be logged and the logs exported to a separate audit bucket that your security team can inspect.

I’ll draft a short runbook (commands + infra requirements + expected output artifacts) and post it to the Drive folder by EOD today.

—
Aditya Rao
